title: Invalidation can lose a race
lesson: A reader can refill an old policy after a newer source commit and cache deletion. In this example the stale entry remains until its TTL expires, measured from the late fill; expiration does not guarantee fresh source data.
transcript: 0.7–2.6s: The Agent asks for the refund policy. The cache holds 30d, answers HIT, and the Agent receives 30d while the database stays untouched.
4.2–5.6s: The Editor saves 14d. The app updates the database to 14d and deletes the cached refund entry while its TTL bar still had time left.

6.7–13.6s: The Agent's next read misses, reads 14d from the database, and the app holds the pending SET 14d. During that pause the Editor saves 7d: the database becomes 7d and the delete finds an empty cache. The held SET 14d then lands with a crash, storing the old value in red; the Agent receives 14d.
15.0–20.5s: Two later reads hit the stale entry. The Agent's badge reads STALE 14d while the database shows 7d in green. The STALE label is the video's annotation, not something a cache reports.
21.3–22.9s: A clock spins with accelerating ticks as the entry's TTL bar runs out; the stale entry disappears.

23.6–31.6s: The next read misses, reads 7d, stores it in green, and the Agent receives 7d with a chime. The resolved state holds, then the diagram fades to black while the title and subtitle remain, matching the opening frame.
limitations: Illustrative scenario: the pause between reading the database and setting the cache stands in for any reordering (pauses, retries, slow networks); no claim is made about how often it happens.

The TTL bounds this entry’s remaining cache residence from its late fill, not data age since the source changed. No hit renews it and no further stale fill occurs here; expiry is not a general freshness guarantee. The lease-token mechanism in Nishtala et al. §3.2.1 prevents stale sets; it is not shown.
The Agent, Editor and refund-policy values are an example; the mechanism applies to any cache-aside reader and writer. The STALE badge is an annotation, not a cache feature.
One key and one cache node; replicated caches and multi-node invalidation are out of scope.
Audio was checked by decoded peak level (-1.8 dBFS), per-cue onset energy and spectrogram, not listened to.
30d, 14d and 7d are example refund-policy values, not cache lifetimes. The draining bar represents the separate TTL.
corrections: Moved cache feedback beside the row so hit/check markers and rings do not obscure policy values.
Enlarged policy, source, badge and packet text to 36px and editor/subtitle to 38px for phone viewing.
Retitled the on-screen mechanism STALE FILL RACE; bounded TTL claims to this entry after the delayed fill.
Pinned rendering resolution to the repository dependency; capped encoder and filter threads at two.
